subject: FinWise — Post-demo: performance targets & load-test coordination
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finwise.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinWise — Post-demo: performance targets & load-test coordination

Alex / Samir — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can schedule the customer-led load test.

Summary of performance targets you mentioned on the call:
- Latency: p95 <= 200 ms for synchronous text generation (50-token responses). p99 target TBD but want to monitor.
- Throughput: sustained 1,000 requests/sec to the endpoints under test (we should confirm exact endpoint paths).
- Concurrency: support ~200 concurrent in-flight requests; connection count estimates: ~250 including control traffic.
- Streaming: yes — you rely on chunked streaming (SSE/HTTP chunked) for partial tokens; we need to ensure streaming behavior and time-to-first-byte meet the p95 target.
- Payload: average prompt size ~1-2k tokens; max context 8k tokens for the test.

What we need from FinWise to run the customer-led load test:
1) Staging/test endpoint and a short-lived API key (or test account) we can use in k6/Locust scripts.
2) IP ranges to allowlist for our load generators (we typically provide a set of IPs but will use the ones you provide if you need tighter controls).
3) Confirmation of a 2-hour test window (smoke, ramp, sustained, cool-down). Suggested window: Tue Apr 12, 10:00-12:00 PT.
4) Any additional auth/network constraints (mutual TLS, header restrictions, WAF rules, etc.).

Our proposed plan (high-level):
- Redwood to run a 15-minute smoke run to verify connectivity, auth, and basic request/response behavior.
- Ramp over 30 minutes to 1,000 RPS (or agreed throughput), hold for 60 minutes, then cool down 15 minutes.
- We'll stream telemetry to a shared dashboard (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput, token/sec, connection stats).

We can use k6 (preferred) or Locust. If you have an existing k6 script, please share; otherwise I can share a starter k6 script and a runbook.

Next steps / asks: please reply with the staging endpoint, a short-lived API key (or a test account we can use), and the IP ranges for allowlisting. Once we have those we'll share the final runbook and k6 script and confirm the window.

Thanks — Logan

--
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: FinWise — Post-demo: performance targets & load-test coordination

Alex — great, thanks for the endpoint and the k6 script. We'll use the IP ranges you listed (35.214.12.0/24, 34.120.8.0/24, 18.162.4.0/24) for the allowlist.

Plan and what we're sending you now:
- Attachment: loadtest_runbook.pdf — step-by-step runbook with timing, monitoring links, and rollback triggers.
- Attachment: redwood_test_account.txt — contains a scoped test key and a short-lived token for the Redwood team to use if you prefer that to the staging-key you created.
- We'll run the smoke at 09:00 PT on Apr 12 for 15 minutes using your staging-key to validate connectivity. After smoke, we'll ramp to 1,000 RPS over 30 minutes, hold for 60 minutes, then cool down 15 minutes.

k6 params we'll run (example):
- vus: ramping from 50 -> 500 -> 1500 (adjusted by concurrency),
- duration: ~2h total (including smoke & cool-down),
- thresholds: http_req_duration p95 < 200ms, http_req_failed rate < 1%

Monitoring & rollback
- We'll publish a realtime dashboard (link in runbook) and tag FinWise contacts. If p95 > 300ms sustained for 5 minutes or error rate > 3% we'll stop the run immediately and do a controlled cool-down.

Confirming: starting smoke at 09:00 PT on Apr 12 works for us. We'll use the staging endpoint you provided for the smoke run and switch to the Redwood-scoped test key only if you ask us to.

Thanks — attaching runbook and test account stub.

--
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
